**SECTION B - COMPOSITION (40 marks)**

Mark distribution: Content and Organisation (12 marks); Expression (16 marks); Accuracy (12 marks).

Choose ONE topic to write on from the list below. You are advised to write clearly and effectively, to spell and punctuate correctly, and to ensure that your writing is appropriate in style and content to the topic chosen. Avoid obscene language and do not disclose your identity. You should write between 450 - 500 words.

questions.enonce_markdown: **g)** Discuss the advantages and disadvantages of employing house-helps.
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Plan**

1. Introduction: define house-helps and say why many families employ them.
2. Advantages: relief for working parents, saved time, care of the home and of the elderly, income for the helper.
3. Disadvantages: insecurity and theft, bad influence, abuse and child labour, cost.
4. A balanced judgement: how to employ a house-help responsibly.
5. Conclusion.

**Model composition (455 words)**

A house-help is a person who is paid to do domestic work such as cooking, washing, cleaning and looking after children. Nowadays, many families in our towns employ house-helps, and this practice has both advantages and disadvantages.

The first advantage is that a house-help gives relief to working parents. When both the father and the mother leave home early to go to work, someone must prepare breakfast, take the children to school and watch over the house. A house-help does this work, and as a result, the parents can concentrate on their jobs without worrying, and their children are not left alone and neglected. Secondly, house-helps save time and energy. A busy mother who returns home tired in the evening finds the house clean and the meal ready, and she can spend the rest of the evening helping her children with their homework. Thirdly, house-helps are of great help to old, sick or disabled persons who cannot take care of themselves. Finally, employing a house-help also benefits the helper, who earns a salary, learns domestic skills and can send money to her family in the village.

However, house-helps also bring a number of problems. First, there is the question of security. A person who is not well known to the family may steal money and valuables, or let thieves into the house. Some house-helps have even harmed the children in their care. Secondly, a house-help may have a bad influence on the children. If she is badly brought up, she may teach them rude language, lies or unhealthy habits, and spend long hours with them in front of the television instead of supervising their studies. Thirdly, many house-helps are young girls and boys who are overworked, underpaid and sometimes beaten or insulted by their employers. In some cases, they are not allowed to go to school, and this is a form of child labour, which the law forbids. Lastly, a house-help can be a financial burden, because the family must feed, house and pay her, and a dishonest one may cost them more than she is worth.

In my opinion, employing a house-help is useful when it is done responsibly. Employers should choose people they can trust, pay them fairly, treat them kindly and, if they are young, allow them to attend school or learn a trade. At the same time, parents should never leave the upbringing of their children entirely in the hands of a house-help.

In conclusion, house-helps can make family life easier, but they can also create problems of security, discipline and justice, and every family must weigh them carefully. The family which treats them with respect and watches over them carefully will enjoy the advantages and avoid most of the disadvantages.

**Marking grid**

| Criterion | Marks | What earns the marks |
|---|---|---|
| Content and Organisation | 12 | Relevant ideas that answer the topic, developed with examples, in clear paragraphs with an introduction and a conclusion |
| Expression | 16 | Varied vocabulary and sentence structures, appropriate style and tone, fluent links between ideas |
| Accuracy | 12 | Correct grammar, tenses, spelling and punctuation |

**Common mistakes**

1. Writing only the advantages or only the disadvantages: the topic asks to discuss both.
2. Using informal language or personal anecdotes instead of an organised discussion.
